title: Quant Certification Artifacts, Pinning Metadata, and Regression Watchtower
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Scope: Define an immutable 'quant certification' artifact and publish workflow used by runtime, console and release pipelines. The artifact must capture: quant scheme (INT8/FP8/GPTQ/AWQ), calibration seed & data fingerprint, deterministic build inputs, compiler flags, kernel hints, measured perf contract (latency p50/p95, throughput at batch sizes), accuracy deltas vs baseline for a curated eval set, and a canonical provenance string for pinning (e.g. model@sha + quant_artifact@v1+checksum).

Goals:
- Produce a machine-readable artifact schema and publishing API for use by Dedicated/Private and Hosted flows.
- Ensure pinning semantics are unambiguous: customers can pin to model+quant artifact version; runtime resolves fallbacks automatically when pinned variant is unavailable.
- Add regression detection ("Watchtower") that compares live telemetry against artifact perf contract and triggers rollbacks or canary throttles when breach probability exceeds threshold.
- Integrate artifact publishing into CI with delta CI gate: block merges that introduce regressed quant artifacts beyond configured tolerances.

Acceptance criteria:
- JSON/YAML artifact schema published to docs + schema registry.
- CI step implemented that runs the artifact through synthetic microbenchmarks and submits a signed artifact to S3/artifact-store.
- Runtime can consume artifact metadata to choose kernels and caching policies, and Console surfaces per-artifact perf summary and pin metadata.
- Watchtower shows alerts on perf deviation > 10% p95 or accuracy delta > 0.8% on golden eval set, with automated canary throttle + optional rollback.

Artifact Format (brief):
- artifact_id: string (semantic version + checksum)
- model_ref: string (model@sha)
